cur:catacombs-sarcophagus-31537.summary: A continuous frieze of tightly packed figures runs across the front: Christ performs miracles among the apostles, and at the right end he rides on a donkey into Jerusalem while a man spreads his garment before him. The relief reads like a pageant of Christ's saving works culminating in his royal entry.
facts: Commons records that the sarcophagus comes from the Coemeterium Maius on the Via Nomentana.
Continuous frieze sarcophagi of this kind were the commonest type of Christian sarcophagus in Constantinian Rome.

wga:zearly/1/4mosaics/2ravenna/5vitale/2.summary: In the golden conch of the apse a youthful, beardless Christ in imperial purple sits on a blue globe above a flowering paradise meadow. He holds a scroll in his left hand and extends a jewelled martyr's crown with his right toward Saint Vitalis, led in by an angel; on the other side a second angel introduces Bishop Ecclesius, who offers a model of the church. This serene image of Christ as ruler of the cosmos, receiving the gifts of martyr and founder, crowns one of the most celebrated mosaic ensembles of the age of Justinian.
facts: Construction of San Vitale began in 526 under Bishop Ecclesius and was completed in 547 under Bishop Maximian, after the Byzantine reconquest of Italy.
Directly below this apse, on its side walls, are the famous panels of Emperor Justinian and Empress Theodora with their courts.
San Vitale is one of eight Ravenna monuments inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
wga:zearly/1/4mosaics/2ravenna/5vitale/2.notes: Title made more descriptive; WGA's 'Christ in the Paradisical Garden' is retained in substance.
